A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same camera-pose refinement work, renamed from GSLoc to GS-CPR. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original localization experiments on 7Scenes, 12Scenes, and Cambridge Landmarks, plus runtime, matcher, exposure-adaptation, and rendering analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds pose-perturbation tests, GLACE refinement results, and expanded matching comparisons in its appendix.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the relative variant's stated translation update from t_hat + s R_rel t_rel to R_rel t_hat + s t_rel. The main 3DGS, ACT, MASt3R, and PnP pipeline remains unchanged. This establishes a revision to the published inference rule, without establishing an implementation change or rerun.

E1.justification: The three datasets remain unchanged. Appendix A.5 adds a controlled input scenario using synthetically perturbed ground-truth initial poses on ShopFacade, extending evaluation beyond pose-estimator outputs. The additional GLACE evaluations reuse existing dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds HLoc with SuperPoint and SuperGlue to the Cambridge comparison; its existing 7Scenes participation is merely relabeled more explicitly. Figure 10 adds ACE-pose-based reference-image retrieval alongside NetVLAD.

E3.justification: Table 4 extends 12Scenes evaluation to median translation/rotation errors and 5cm/5-degree recall. New experiments independently perturb rotation and translation on ShopFacade and evaluate GLACE as an initializer. Figure 10 switches the rendered-view initializer from DFNet to ACE. These are extensions within retained benchmarks, without a documented change to the main training budget.

E4.justification: Appendix A.5 introduces a systematic initial-pose sensitivity study over rotational and translational perturbations, supported by Tables 10–11 and a failure example in Figure 12. Figure 10 expands a single retrieval illustration into three scene comparisons with correspondence counts. These substantially extend robustness and diagnostic evidence beyond the retained ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions average runtime measurements over 1,000 runs. v3 introduces no new seed counts, repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added perturbation results remain point estimates.

E6.justification: v3 adds GLACE refinement results across all three benchmarks, perturbation outcomes, matching counts, and Cambridge HLoc results. Table 4 adds aggregate 12Scenes metrics but removes the per-scene 2cm/2-degree scores, retaining their averages. Table 3 revises GLACE's Cambridge scores, changing its reported average from 13cm/0.32 degrees to 14cm/0.32 degrees. Table 6 changes DFNet plus the relative variant from 0.07 to 0.08 seconds and ACE plus refinement from 0.18 to 0.19 seconds. Most retained headline accuracy results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 3 revises the mathematical pose composition by changing which translation is multiplied by the relative rotation. This is an algebraically substantive correction, rather than equivalent notation. Equations 1–2 are retained, and neither version contains a separate theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: one-shot refinement using 3DGS and MASt3R, exposure adaptation, improved APR/SCR localization, greater accuracy and speed than NeRF-based optimization, and state-of-the-art results on two indoor datasets. Renaming and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix A.5 newly identifies failures caused by inaccurate initial poses and insufficient image overlap, and acknowledges difficulties reconstructing large scenes. Appendix A.3 expands the explanation of metric depth, global scale, and synthesized versus retrieved reference views. Appendix A.6 distinguishes strong indoor GLACE improvements from mainly rotational gains on Cambridge. These materially expand applicability boundaries and mechanism interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 specifies HLoc's SuperPoint/SuperGlue configuration and attributes the revised Cambridge GLACE results to official models. It also changes the runtime GPU designation from GTX 4090 to RTX 4090 and revises the COLMAP-model provenance wording in Appendix A.1. These are limited documentation changes; the principal hyperparameters and project-page access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds DeTone et al. (2018) for SuperPoint and Jiao et al. (2024), LiteVLoc, as a depth-camera-based approach contrasted with its metric-depth rendering. The main related-work taxonomy and positioning remain intact; the Air-HLoc reference update is bibliographic.

P1.justification: GSLoc becomes GS-CPR throughout, publication and author formatting change, and citations receive consistent parentheses. Appendix A.3 gains explanatory prose and A.5–A.6 are added, but the existing narrative and section sequence are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 10 is rebuilt as a full-page, three-scene correspondence comparison; Figure 12 and Tables 10–13 are added. Table 4 changes from a scene-by-scene layout to an aggregate multi-metric comparison, and Figure 3 explicitly marks the scale path and highlights the variant's differing component. These substantially expand and restructure the evidence displays, alongside relocation of retained material.

improvement.justification: v3 improves the paper through the corrected pose-composition equation, explicit failure analysis, controlled perturbation tests, and broader comparator and initializer evidence. The gain is limited by removing per-scene 12Scenes results and retaining Appendix A.3's broad HLoc-superiority statement despite the newly added Cambridge comparison favoring HLoc. Overall, the additions improve support and clarify applicability while leaving the core findings largely unchanged.
